sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca hateṣu sarvasainyeṣu sauptike tai rathais tribhiḥ śocan yudhiṣṭhiro rājā dāśārham idam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When all the troops had been slain in the night-massacre by those three warriors, King Yudhiṣṭhira, grieving, spoke thus to the descendant of the Dāśārhas:

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu kṛṣṇa pāpena kṣudreṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā drauṇinā nihatāḥ sarve mama putrā mahārathāḥ
english: How, O Kṛṣṇa, were all my sons, those mighty warriors, slain by the wicked, base, tireless-handed son of Droṇa?

sanskrit: tathā kṛtāstrā vikrāntāḥ sahasraśatayodhinaḥ drupadasyātmajāś caiva droṇaputreṇa pātitāḥ
english: Likewise those skilled in arms, valiant, each a match for a hundred thousand foes, and the sons of Drupada as well—how were they all struck down by Droṇa's son?

sanskrit: yasya droṇo maheṣvāso na prādād āhave mukham taṃ jaghne rathināṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ kathaṃ nu saḥ
english: How did he slay Dhṛṣṭadyumna, foremost of chariot-warriors, before whom Droṇa, the great archer, would not show his face in battle?

sanskrit: kiṃ nu tena kṛtaṃ karma tathāyuktaṃ nararṣabha yad ekaḥ śibiraṃ sarvam avadhīn no guroḥ sutaḥ
english: What deed, so beyond his power, did the teacher's son perform, O bull among men, that single-handed he destroyed our whole camp?

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca nūnaṃ sa devadevānām īśvareśvaram avyayam jagāma śaraṇaṃ drauṇir ekas tenāvadhīd bahūn
english: Vāsudeva said: Surely the son of Droṇa took refuge with the imperishable Lord of lords, the God of gods; therefore alone he slew the many.

sanskrit: prasanno hi mahādevo dadyād amaratām api vīryaṃ ca giriśo dadyād yenendram api śātayet
english: For when gracious, Mahādeva would grant even immortality, and the Mountain-dweller would grant such valor that one might lay even Indra low.

sanskrit: vedāhaṃ hi mahādevaṃ tattvena bharatarṣabha yāni cāsya purāṇāni karmāṇi vividhāny uta
english: For I know Mahādeva in his very essence, O bull of the Bhāratas, and the many ancient deeds that are his.

sanskrit: ādir eṣa hi bhūtānāṃ madhyam antaś ca bhārata viceṣṭate jagac cedaṃ sarvam asyaiva karmaṇā
english: For he is the beginning of all beings, their middle and their end, O Bhārata; and this whole world moves by his action alone.

sanskrit: evaṃ sisṛkṣur bhūtāni dadarśa prathamaṃ vibhuḥ pitāmaho 'bravīc cainaṃ bhūtāni sṛja māciram
english: Thus, desiring to create beings, the Lord first beheld him, and the Grandsire said to him: Create the beings without delay.

sanskrit: harikeśas tathety uktvā bhūtānāṃ doṣadarśivān dīrghakālaṃ tapas tepe magno 'mbhasi mahātapāḥ
english: Saying "So be it," Harikeśa, foreseeing the flaws of beings, performed austerities for a long time, that great ascetic, sunk beneath the waters.

sanskrit: sumahāntaṃ tataḥ kālaṃ pratīkṣyainaṃ pitāmahaḥ sraṣṭāraṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ sasarja manasāparam
english: After waiting for him a very long while, the Grandsire created from his mind another to be the maker of all beings.

sanskrit: so 'bravīt pitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā giriśaṃ magnam ambhasi yadi me nāgrajas tv anyas tataḥ srakṣyāmy ahaṃ prajāḥ
english: Seeing his father the Mountain-dweller sunk beneath the waters, this one said: If no other is born before me, then I shall create the creatures.

sanskrit: tam abravīt pitā nāsti tvad anyaḥ puruṣo 'grajaḥ sthāṇur eṣa jale magno visrabdhaḥ kuru vai kṛtim
english: His father said to him: There is no other being born before you. This is Sthāṇu, sunk in the water; with confidence, do your work.

sanskrit: sa bhūtāny asṛjat sapta dakṣādīṃs tu prajāpatīn yair imaṃ vyakarot sarvaṃ bhūtagrāmaṃ caturvidham
english: He created the seven beings, the lords of creatures beginning with Dakṣa, by whom he brought forth this whole fourfold host of beings.

sanskrit: tāḥ sṛṣṭamātrāḥ kṣudhitāḥ prajāḥ sarvāḥ prajāpatim bibhakṣayiṣavo rājan sahasā prādravaṃs tadā
english: No sooner were they created than all the creatures, famished and eager to devour, rushed at once upon the Lord of creatures, O king.

sanskrit: sa bhakṣyamāṇas trāṇārthī pitāmaham upādravat ābhyo māṃ bhagavān pātu vṛttir āsāṃ vidhīyatām
english: Being devoured, and seeking protection, he ran to the Grandsire: May the Blessed One save me from these; let some means of sustenance be ordained for them.

sanskrit: tatas tābhyo dadāv annam oṣadhīḥ sthāvarāṇi ca jaṅgamāni ca bhūtāni durbalāni balīyasām
english: Then he gave them food: the herbs, the things that stand fixed, and the moving creatures—the weaker as nourishment for the stronger.

sanskrit: vihitānnāḥ prajās tās tu jagmus tuṣṭā yathāgatam tato vavṛdhire rājan prītimatyaḥ svayoniṣu
english: Their food thus appointed, those creatures went away contented as they had come, and then, well pleased, O king, they multiplied each in their own kind.

sanskrit: bhūtagrāme vivṛddhe tu tuṣṭe lokagurāv api udatiṣṭhaj jalāj jyeṣṭhaḥ prajāś cemā dadarśa saḥ
english: When the host of beings had grown and the teacher of the worlds was satisfied, the elder one rose up from the waters and beheld these creatures.

sanskrit: bahurūpāḥ prajā dṛṣṭvā vivṛddhāḥ svena tejasā cukrodha bhagavān rudro liṅgaṃ svaṃ cāpy avidhyata
english: Seeing the creatures, of many forms, grown great by their own power, the blessed Rudra grew wroth and tore out his own emblem.

sanskrit: tat praviddhaṃ tadā bhūmau tathaiva pratyatiṣṭhata tam uvācāvyayo brahmā vacobhiḥ śamayann iva
english: Cast upon the earth, it stood there fixed even so; and the imperishable Brahmā spoke to him, as if calming him with words:

sanskrit: kiṃ kṛtaṃ salile śarva cirakālaṃ sthitena te kimarthaṃ caitad utpāṭya bhūmau liṅgaṃ praveritam
english: What have you done, O Śarva, abiding so long in the water? And why have you torn out this emblem and flung it upon the earth?

sanskrit: so 'bravīj jātasaṃrambhas tadā lokagurur gurum prajāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ pareṇemāḥ kiṃ kariṣyāmy anena vai
english: Then the teacher of the worlds, his anger kindled, said to his elder: These creatures have been created by another; what now shall I do with this?

sanskrit: tapasādhigataṃ cānnaṃ prajārthaṃ me pitāmaha oṣadhyaḥ parivarteran yathaiva satataṃ prajāḥ
english: The food I won by austerity for the sake of the creatures, O Grandsire—let the herbs renew themselves perpetually, even as the creatures do.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu saṃkruddho jagāma vimanā bhavaḥ girer muñjavataḥ pādaṃ tapas taptuṃ mahātapāḥ
english: Having spoken thus, Bhava, enraged and downcast, that great ascetic, went to the foot of Mount Muñjavat to perform his austerities.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca tato devayuge 'tīte devā vai samakalpayan yajñaṃ vedapramāṇena vidhivad yaṣṭum īpsavaḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: Then, when the age of the gods had passed, the gods made ready a sacrifice, desiring to offer it duly according to the measure of the Vedas.

sanskrit: kalpayām āsur avyagrā deśān yajñocitāṃs tataḥ bhāgārhā devatāś caiva yajñiyaṃ dravyam eva ca
english: Unhurried, they appointed the places fit for the sacrifice, the deities worthy of shares, and the materials of the offering as well.

sanskrit: tā vai rudram ajānantyo yāthātathyena devatāḥ nākalpayanta devasya sthāṇor bhāgaṃ narādhipa
english: But those deities, not knowing Rudra as he truly is, appointed no share for the god Sthāṇu, O lord of men.

sanskrit: so 'kalpyamāne bhāge tu kṛttivāsā makhe 'maraiḥ tarasā bhāgam anvicchan dhanur ādau sasarja ha
english: And when no share was appointed for him by the immortals in the sacrifice, the One clad in hide, swiftly seeking his portion, first of all fashioned a bow.

sanskrit: lokayajñaḥ kriyāyajño gṛhayajñaḥ sanātanaḥ pañcabhūtamayo yajño nṛyajñaś caiva pañcamaḥ
english: The world-sacrifice, the rite-sacrifice, the eternal household-sacrifice, the sacrifice made of the five elements, and the man-sacrifice as the fifth—

sanskrit: lokayajñena yajñaiṣī kapardī vidadhe dhanuḥ dhanuḥ sṛṣṭam abhūt tasya pañcakiṣkupramāṇataḥ
english: of these, the matted-haired one, desiring the sacrifice, fashioned his bow from the world-sacrifice; and the bow he made measured five cubits.

sanskrit: vaṣaṭkāro 'bhavaj jyā tu dhanuṣas tasya bhārata yajñāṅgāni ca catvāri tasya saṃhanane 'bhavan
english: The sacred utterance Vaṣaṭ became the bowstring of that bow, O Bhārata, and four limbs of the sacrifice became its frame.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahādevas tad upādāya kārmukam ājagāmātha tatraiva yatra devāḥ samījire
english: Then, enraged, Mahādeva took up that bow and came to the very place where the gods were performing their sacrifice.

sanskrit: tam āttakārmukaṃ dṛṣṭvā brahmacāriṇam avyayam vivyathe pṛthivī devī parvatāś ca cakampire
english: Seeing him, the imperishable celibate, with bow in hand, the goddess Earth trembled and the mountains quaked.

sanskrit: na vavau pavanaś caiva nāgnir jajvāla caidhitaḥ vyabhramac cāpi saṃvignaṃ divi nakṣatramaṇḍalam
english: The wind ceased to blow, and the fire, though fed, would not blaze; and the circle of stars, in agitation, wandered confused in the sky.

sanskrit: na babhau bhāskaraś cāpi somaḥ śrīmuktamaṇḍalaḥ timireṇākulaṃ sarvam ākāśaṃ cābhavad vṛtam
english: The sun shone no more, and the moon's disk lost its splendor; and the whole sky, troubled, was veiled in darkness.

sanskrit: abhibhūtās tato devā viṣayān na prajajñire na pratyabhāc ca yajñas tān vedā babhraṃśire tadā
english: Overwhelmed, the gods could no longer perceive their objects; the sacrifice shone for them no more, and the Vedas slipped away from them then.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa yajñaṃ raudreṇa vivyādha hṛdi patriṇā apakrāntas tato yajño mṛgo bhūtvā sapāvakaḥ
english: Then with a fierce winged arrow he pierced the Sacrifice through the heart, and the Sacrifice, becoming a deer together with the fire, fled away.

sanskrit: sa tu tenaiva rūpeṇa divaṃ prāpya vyarocata anvīyamāno rudreṇa yudhiṣṭhira nabhastale
english: And in that very form it reached the sky and shone, pursued by Rudra across the vault of heaven, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: apakrānte tato yajñe saṃjñā na pratyabhāt surān naṣṭasaṃjñeṣu deveṣu na prajñāyata kiṃ cana
english: When the Sacrifice had fled, consciousness returned no more to the gods, and with the gods bereft of sense nothing could be discerned.

sanskrit: tryambakaḥ savitur bāhū bhagasya nayane tathā pūṣṇaś ca daśanān kruddho dhanuṣkoṭyā vyaśātayat
english: In his wrath the three-eyed one, with the tip of his bow, struck off the arms of Savitṛ, the eyes of Bhaga, and the teeth of Pūṣan.

sanskrit: prādravanta tato devā yajñāṅgāni ca sarvaśaḥ ke cit tatraiva ghūrṇanto gatāsava ivābhavan
english: Then the gods and the limbs of the sacrifice fled in every direction, and some, reeling on the spot, became as though their breath had left them.

sanskrit: sa tu vidrāvya tat sarvaṃ śitikaṇṭho 'vahasya ca avaṣṭabhya dhanuṣkoṭiṃ rurodha vibudhāṃs tataḥ
english: And the blue-throated one, having scattered all that and laughing aloud, leaned upon the tip of his bow and held the gods at bay.

sanskrit: tato vāg amarair uktā jyāṃ tasya dhanuṣo 'cchinat atha tat sahasā rājaṃś chinnajyaṃ visphurad dhanuḥ
english: Then a voice uttered by the immortals cut the string of his bow; and at once, O king, its string severed, the bow sprang back quivering.

sanskrit: tato vidhanuṣaṃ devā devaśreṣṭham upāgaman śaraṇaṃ saha yajñena prasādaṃ cākarot prabhuḥ
english: Then the gods, together with the Sacrifice, came for refuge to the foremost of gods, now bereft of his bow; and the Lord showed them his grace.

sanskrit: tataḥ prasanno bhagavān prāsyat kopaṃ jalāśaye sa jalaṃ pāvako bhūtvā śoṣayaty aniśaṃ prabho
english: Then the gracious Lord cast his wrath into a body of water; and that wrath, becoming fire, dries up the water without ceasing, O lord.

sanskrit: bhagasya nayane caiva bāhū ca savitus tathā prādāt pūṣṇaś ca daśanān punar yajñaṃ ca pāṇḍava
english: And he gave back the eyes of Bhaga, the arms of Savitṛ, and the teeth of Pūṣan, and the Sacrifice once more, O son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvam idaṃ svasthaṃ babhūva punar eva ha sarvāṇi ca havīṃṣy asya devā bhāgam akalpayan
english: Then all this became whole again, and the gods appointed for him all the oblations as his share.

sanskrit: tasmin kruddhe 'bhavat sarvam asvasthaṃ bhuvanaṃ vibho prasanne ca punaḥ svasthaṃ sa prasanno 'sya vīryavān
english: When he was wroth, the whole world became unwell, O lord; and when he was gracious, it grew whole again—such is the power of him when his grace is won.

sanskrit: tatas te nihatāḥ sarve tava putrā mahārathāḥ anye ca bahavaḥ śūrāḥ pāñcālāś ca sahānugāḥ
english: It was through his grace, then, that all your sons, those mighty warriors, were slain, and many other heroes too, and the Pāñcālas with their followers.

sanskrit: na tan manasi kartavyaṃ na hi tad drauṇinā kṛtam mahādevaprasādaḥ sa kuru kāryam anantaram
english: You must not take this to heart, for it was not the son of Droṇa who did it: that was the grace of Mahādeva. Now do the duty that comes next.
